developer: Dr. Faranak "Fara" Kamangar MD, board-certified dermatologist, Department Chair, Palo Alto Medical Foundation.
version: Not versioned; a learned language model based on dermatology knowledge from more than 3,000 peer-reviewed articles and texts, not a versioned software release.
availability: Available for anyone to use online.
summary: DermGPT is a dermatology-focused AI chatbot, developed by a board-certified dermatologist, that allows dermatologists and staff to ask natural-language questions and receive cited answers drawn from more than 3,000 peer-reviewed dermatology articles and texts. It is intended as a practice-management and knowledge-access assistant rather than a stand-alone clinical decision maker.
medicalPurpose: Simplify everyday administrative tasks associated with dermatology practice management and improve access to dermatology knowledge, as an assistant rather than a stand-alone decision maker; does not replace medical care or clinical decision-making.
acceptableInput: Natural-language prompts entered into the web chat app, e.g. questions about diagnoses, treatments, prior authorization letters, or differential diagnosis for a described presentation.
output: Natural-language text answers with citations, drawn from a learned language model trained on more than 3,000 peer-reviewed dermatology articles and texts; outputs include text-based answers, patient handouts, and authorization letters.
roleInDecisionMaking: A complementary tool rather than a sole decision-maker; the full underlying dataset is not fully disclosed, so healthcare professionals should continue independent clinical judgment to mitigate potential bias.
intendedUsers: Dermatologists and dermatology practice staff (RNs, MAs, ancillary staff), as well as medical students, residents, and researchers. No specialized technical knowledge is required; preferred use is by medical professionals, though the developer notes users should proofread all AI-generated content for accuracy.
targetPatientPopulation: Not applicable to patients directly; intended for use by medical professionals rather than for a specific patient population.
knownPerformanceLimitations: Not a substitute for professional medical advice; limited to its database of peer-reviewed publications; like all AI tools, lacks human creativity and intuition and is most effective when paired with a dermatology provider or staff who complement it with higher-level clinical judgment.
skinTypeRepresentationEquity: Not specified; the underlying peer-reviewed literature dataset's representativeness across skin tones/ethnicities has not been disclosed, so it is unclear whether the training corpus is inclusive of people of color.
requiredClinicianOversight: No formal clinician oversight requirement, as this is an informational AI chatbot rather than a diagnostic device; standard risks apply, including potential for incorrect medical advice and bias if underlying literature is not inclusive. Users are advised to proofread all AI-generated content.
modelType: Informative large language model (LLM) trained on dermatology literature.

trainingData.description: Trained on dermatology knowledge from more than 3,000 peer-reviewed articles and texts, including medical literature, clinical trials/studies, drug formulary information, expert consensus/reviews, and educational resources; full dataset composition is not fully disclosed.

modelDevelopmentAndValidation.description: Developed using peer-reviewed dermatology literature and other published sources; no independent validation study identified.

performance.summary: Developer-reported: in the developer's own practice, DermGPT saved approximately 30-60 minutes per day previously spent on EHR documentation, allowing clinic days to finish earlier; no independent, peer-reviewed performance studies identified.

performanceEvaluationLimitations: The full training dataset is not fully disclosed, so it is unknown whether the peer-reviewed literature used is representative of the entire patient population; no independent validation has been published; reported time-savings are anecdotal/developer-reported.
ongoingMonitoringPlan: Continuously updated and improved by the developer, intended to remain current with new dermatology literature.
scheduledUpdates: Continuous updates per the developer; no fixed schedule disclosed.
